params.name: order_by
params.description: Sort order of returned clusters.

params.description: Page number to return for clusters, from the paginated results.

params.name: page_size
params.description: Maximum number of clusters per page.

params.name: name
params.description: Name to filter on, only clusters containing this substring in their name will be returned.

params.name: status
params.description: Status to filter on, only clusters with this status will be returned.

params.name: type
params.description: Type to filter on, only clusters with this type will be returned.

params.name: private_network_id
params.description: Private Network ID to filter on, only clusters within this Private Network will be returned.

items.docs: Update information on a specific Kubernetes cluster. You can update details such as its name, description, tags and configuration. To upgrade a cluster, you will need to use the dedicated endpoint.

info.name: List available cluster types for a cluster

params.name: region
params.description: The region you want to target

params.name: cluster_id
params.description: Cluster ID for which the available Kubernetes types will be listed.

items.docs: List the cluster types that a specific Kubernetes cluster is allowed to switch to.

info.name: List available versions for a Cluster

params.name: region
params.description: The region you want to target

params.name: cluster_id
params.description: Cluster ID for which the available Kubernetes versions will be listed.

items.docs: List the versions that a specific Kubernetes cluster is allowed to upgrade to. Results will include every patch version greater than the current patch, as well as one minor version ahead of the current version. Any upgrade skipping a minor version will not work.

info.name: Download the kubeconfig for a Cluster

params.name: region
params.description: The region you want to target

params.name: cluster_id
params.description: Cluster ID for which to download the kubeconfig.

params.name: redacted
params.description: Hide the legacy token from the kubeconfig.

items.docs:
Download the Kubernetes cluster config file (also known as `kubeconfig`) for a specific cluster to use it with `kubectl`.
Tip: add `?dl=1` at the end of the URL to directly retrieve the base64 decoded kubeconfig. If you choose not to, the kubeconfig will be base64 encoded.

info.name: Reset the admin token of a Cluster

params.name: region
params.description: The region you want to target

params.name: cluster_id
params.description: Cluster ID on which the admin token will be renewed.

items.docs: Reset the admin token for a specific Kubernetes cluster. This will revoke the old admin token (which will not be usable afterwards) and create a new one. Note that you will need to download the kubeconfig again to keep interacting with the cluster.

items.docs: Change the type of a specific Kubernetes cluster. To see the possible values you can enter for the `type` field, [list available cluster types](#list-available-cluster-types-for-a-cluster).
